# Bringing statistical clarity to neural networks

I am a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Limerick. My work treats neural networks as statistical models—making their structure more parsimonious, their uncertainty more explicit, and their results easier to interpret.

::: {.section-shell #research}
<p class="section-kicker">Research</p>

## Neural networks through a statistical lens

My research sits at the intersection of statistical modelling and machine learning. I develop practical methods that retain the flexibility of neural networks while supporting the questions statisticians care about: which variables matter, how complex should a model be, and how certain are its conclusions?

::: {.focus-grid}
::: {.focus-card}
<span class="card-index">01</span>

### Model selection

Likelihood- and information-criterion-based approaches for selecting inputs and architecture, with an emphasis on parsimony and reproducibility.
:::

::: {.focus-card}
<span class="card-index">02</span>

### Statistical inference

Methods for hypothesis testing and uncertainty quantification that make neural-network parameters and predictions more informative.
:::

::: {.focus-card}
<span class="card-index">03</span>

### Interpretation

Covariate-effect visualisations and open-source tools that help researchers inspect fitted neural networks as statistical models.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.section-shell .selected-work}
<p class="section-kicker">Selected work</p>

## Recent research

::: {.work-grid}
::: {.work-card .work-card-featured}
<p class="work-meta">Statistical Modelling · 2025</p>

### A statistical modelling approach to feedforward neural network model selection

A BIC-based framework for selecting both input variables and hidden-node complexity in feedforward neural networks.

[Read the paper {{< fa arrow-right >}}](https://doi.org/10.1177/1471082X241258261){.text-link}
:::

::: {.work-card}
<p class="work-meta">arXiv · 2023</p>

### Feedforward neural networks as statistical models

Hypothesis tests, uncertainty quantification, and covariate-effect plots for more interpretable neural-network analyses.

[Read the preprint {{< fa arrow-right >}}](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.08139){.text-link}
:::
:::

### interpretnn

Statistical inference and interpretation for fitted neural networks, with support for models from `nnet`, `neuralnet`, Keras, ANN, and torch.

[Package website](https://andrew-mcinerney.github.io/interpretnn/) · [Source](https://github.com/andrew-mcinerney/interpretnn)
:::

::: {.software-card}
::: {.software-mark}
`R`
:::

### selectnn

Stepwise BIC-based variable and architecture selection for feedforward neural networks fitted with `nnet`.

[Package website](https://andrew-mcinerney.github.io/selectnn/) · [Source](https://github.com/andrew-mcinerney/selectnn)
:::
